raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- sparse_pa.py: call AITER's Gluon paged attention with `compute_type=q.dtype` on an FP8 KV cache, so Q and the softmax weights stay in BF16 and only K/V are upcast from FP8.
- test_minimax_m3.py: first numerical test of the AITER sparse attention path on an FP8 cache, against fp32 attention on the dequantized cache with an error bound derived from the BF16 roundings.

With an FP8 KV cache the MiniMax-M3 ROCm sparse attention asked AITER for FP8 compute without a query scale, so the kernel rounded the BF16 query and the softmax weights to e4m3. Q's range is not the problem (on gsm8k traffic |q| stays under 14, far below 448, and a per-token query scale changes nothing); e4m3's 3-bit mantissa is. Rounding Q alone moves the attention output by 2% (median head) to 7% (median worst head per token) against an fp32 reference on the same cache. With BF16 compute the error drops to 0.2-0.3%. The kernel is 2-7% slower below about 4K rows and as fast above, which does not show end to end, and gsm8k does not move, so this improves precision and does not fix an accuracy regression.

MI355X, MiniMax-M3 at TP4 (16 query heads and 1 KV head per rank), FP8 KV cache. Before forces `compute_type` back to FP8; after is this PR. Both arms run on identical inputs.

Attention output error against fp32 attention on the dequantized cache. Inputs match MiniMax-M3's statistics (Q RMS 1.5 from the per-head QK norm, logits spread over about +-10); 64 rows x 16 heads per case:

| keys attended | before: median / worst head / p99 | after: median / worst head / p99 |
|---|---|---|
| 512 | 4.96% / 11.3% / 13.5% | 0.24% / 0.28% / 0.29% |
| 2048 | 5.82% / 11.2% / 13.5% | 0.24% / 0.28% / 0.29% |

Kernel time in us, 2048 keys per row, HIP graph replay over page sets larger than the LLC, median of 3 runs:

| rows | before | after | after / before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.4 | 7.8 | 1.06x |
| 16 | 7.7 | 8.1 | 1.06x |
| 64 | 11.9 | 12.2 | 1.03x |
| 256 | 30.9 | 31.6 | 1.02x |
| 1024 | 101.9 | 109.4 | 1.07x |
| 4096 | 398.2 | 398.1 | 1.00x |
| 8192 | 778.0 | 777.1 | 1.00x |

End to end, MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 (`vllm serve ... -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --language-model-only`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot flexible-extract, 10 runs (mean / sd) | 0.8840 / 0.0075 | 0.8798 / 0.0060 |
| `vllm bench serve` 1K/1K c=32, tok/s (2 runs) | 2594 | 2570 |
| `vllm bench serve` 8K/1K c=16, tok/s | 1173 | 1167 |
| `vllm bench serve` 32K/1K c=8, tok/s | 407 | 408 |

The GSM8K difference is not significant (Welch t -1.40; per question, 222 are solved less often and 228 more often), and the same code varies by up to 3% in throughput between server runs.

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py -k fp8_kv_matches_fp32_reference   # MI355X
2 passed                                                       # this PR
2 failed: row 0: max err / bound 9.99 and 11.79                # compute_type reverted to fp8
```

No open PR changes this kernel's compute type (searched `compute_type sparse_pa minimax`); #64198 touches the MiniMax-M3 ROCm path but not `compute_type`.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

nodes.body:
Low-concurrency latency check, since c=32 throughput can hide a per-step cost. MI355X, MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 at TP4, FP8 KV cache, same serve flags and env as above. Before forces `compute_type` back to FP8. `vllm bench serve` random 1K/1K, `--ignore-eos`, c=1, 16 prompts per run, 6 runs per arm in alternating order, with the two arms swapped between the GPU halves after 3 runs.

| | before (FP8 compute) | after (BF16 compute) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean TPOT (ms) | 6.294 | 6.345 | +0.82% |
| p99 ITL (ms) | 6.554 | 6.605 | +0.77% |
| median E2EL (ms) | 6582 | 6633 | +0.79% |
| output tok/s | 155.6 | 154.4 | -0.78% |
| median TTFT (ms) | 142.6 | 141.9 | noise |

So the kernel slowdown does show end to end at low concurrency: about 50 us per decode step. Every BF16 run was slower than every FP8 run (max FP8 TPOT 6.299 ms, min BF16 6.339 ms), on both GPU layouts (+0.94% / +0.70%). Run-to-run spread is about 0.005 ms. This is the precision-for-latency trade, and I'll update the description, which currently says it doesn't show end to end.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #98820](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98820) for commit `fde9708ea438`.

ℹ️ This PR is 262 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `fde9708ea438` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

Overall it makes sense, but it just seems like a precision/latency tradeoff. If there is some demonstrable accuracy hit that we can show then I think it would justify the small perf hit (like a long-context benchmark)

There was no issue with any test group. FP8 compute here was never a measured tradeoff. It came in with the initial AITER sparse PA (#47287), which benchmarked the whole path against Triton (BF16 Q/P) and never compared FP8 vs BF16 compute. It also passes query_scale=None, while AITER documents a query scale as required for FP8 compute. Measured now, against fp32 attention on the same FP8 cache:  
- FP8 compute: 5-6% median head error, up to 20% worst head (I did add a new test fail that demonstrates 100/100 failure)
- BF16 compute: ≤0.33% (same test has 100/100 pass rate)
- Cost: +0.8% TPOT at c=1 (~50 µs/step), flat at higher concurrency, GSM8K unchanged
 
So MiniMax-M3's own Triton sparse kernel keeps Q/P in BF16, so this path was the outlier within the model, and nobody had ever priced the trade. The new test now guards it in CI. So my gut tells me that maybe there was some aggressive optimization on perf and this setting was hardcoded, to squeeze that .8% perf boost.

Ran it properly. Short version: not a bug, but fp8 Q/P does cost a bit of fidelity, consistently.

Setup: MXFP4 M3, TP4, fp8 KV, mono off. Old (fp8 Q/P) vs this PR (bf16 Q/P), plus a bf16-KV reference and repeat servers.

- Teacher-forced PG19 (24 books, prompt logprobs up to 64K, so this is the prefill call, same kernel/setting as decode): fp8 Q/P raises NLL by 0.003 nats/token at 64K (+0.3% ppl, 95% CI 0.0016-0.0046, 22/24 books), and KL to the bf16-KV reference by 0.0034 (24/24 books). For scale, fp8 KV by itself adds ~0.0017, so the fp8 cast costs roughly 2-3x what fp8 KV does. Same numbers on a second pair of fresh servers with the GPUs swapped.
- It's small next to run-to-run noise (identical runs differ at KL ~0.07 even with bf16 KV). It shows up because it goes the same way on every book, not because it's big.
- Doesn't grow with context, which makes sense since every sparse layer attends a fixed 2048 keys.
- No task-level hit: RULER NIAH at 32K+64K is ~100% on both (3 misses out of 1600, 2 of them on the bf16 side, p=1), and gsm8k was flat.

So I'd call it a precision fix, not a bug fix: closer to the reference for ~50us/step at c=1 when mono is off, no measurable accuracy change on tasks..

files.patch:
@@ -2422,6 +2422,93 @@ def test_aiter_sparse_pa_rejects_multiple_kv_heads(monkeypatch):
     assert backend.get_builder_cls().__name__ == "MiniMaxM3SparseAiterPAMetadataBuilder"
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(),
+    reason="MiniMax-M3 AITER sparse PA is ROCm-only",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("context_len", [200, 2048], ids=["one-shot", "split"])
+def test_aiter_sparse_pa_fp8_kv_matches_fp32_reference(context_len):
+    """FP8 KV must leave Q and P in BF16.
+
+    Against fp32 attention on the dequantized cache, only BF16 roundings of P,
+    of the per-partition outputs and of the output remain (2^-9 each), so
+    |out - ref| <= 2^-8 * sum_i p_i |v_i| + 2^-9 * |ref|. The test allows
+    twice that. Casting Q to e4m3 (2^-4) moves logits of magnitude ~10 by
+    ~0.1 and exceeds it.
+    """
+    pytest.importorskip("aiter")
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.sparse_pa import (
+        ASM_PAGE_SIZE,
+        minimax_m3_sparse_attn_decode_aiter,
+    )
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version
+
+    if get_cdna_version() not in (3, 4):
+        pytest.skip("AITER Gluon paged attention needs CDNA3 or CDNA4")
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    fp8 = current_platform.fp8_dtype()
+    num_tokens, num_heads, x = 4, 16, 16
+    pages = (context_len + ASM_PAGE_SIZE - 1) // ASM_PAGE_SIZE
+    num_pages = num_tokens * pages + 3
+    # Q has the RMS (~1.5) the model's per-head QK norm gives; K * 2 spreads
+    # the logits over about +-10, as measured on MiniMax-M3.
+    q = (1.5 * torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda")).bfloat16()
+    k = 2 * torch.randn(num_pages * ASM_PAGE_SIZE, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda")
+    v = torch.randn(num_pages * ASM_PAGE_SIZE, HEAD_DIM, device="cuda")
+    k_scale = (k.abs().amax() / torch.finfo(fp8).max).reshape(1)
+    v_scale = (v.abs().amax() / torch.finfo(fp8).max).reshape(1)
+    k8, v8 = (k / k_scale).to(fp8), (v / v_scale).to(fp8)
+    k_cache = (
+        k8.view(num_pages, ASM_PAGE_SIZE, HEAD_DIM // x, x)
+        .permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+        .contiguous()
+        .unsqueeze(1)
+    )
+    v_cache = (
+        v8.view(num_pages, ASM_PAGE_SIZE // x, x, HEAD_DIM)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 2)
+        .contiguous()
+        .unsqueeze(1)
+    )
+    block_table = (
+        torch.randperm(num_pages, device="cuda")[: num_tokens * pages]
+        .view(num_tokens, pages)
+        .int()
+    )
+    context_lens = torch.tensor(
+        [context_len - 7 * i for i in range(num_tokens)],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    sm_scale = HEAD_DIM**-0.5
+    out = torch.empty_like(q)
+    minimax_m3_sparse_attn_decode_aiter(
+        q,
+        k_cache,
+        v_cache,
+        None,
+        None,
+        None,
+        1,
+        sm_scale,
+        out,
+        k_scale=k_scale,
+        v_scale=v_scale,
+        sparse_block_table=block_table,
+        sparse_context_lens=context_lens,
+    )
+
+    kd, vd = k8.float() * k_scale, v8.float() * v_scale
+    offsets = torch.arange(ASM_PAGE_SIZE, device="cuda")
+    for t, n in enumerate(context_lens.tolist()):
+        tokens = (block_table[t, :, None] * ASM_PAGE_SIZE + offsets).flatten()[:n]
+        p = torch.softmax(q[t].float() @ kd[tokens].T * sm_scale, dim=-1)
+        ref = p @ vd[tokens]
+        bound = 2 * (2**-8 * (p @ vd[tokens].abs()) + 2**-9 * ref.abs())
+        err = (out[t].float() - ref).abs()
+        assert (err <= bound).all(), f"row {t}: max err / bound {(err / bound).max()}"
+
+
 def test_msa_indexer_requires_the_aiter_attend(monkeypatch):
     """The top-k emits the attend's page table, so it needs that attend.

@@ -532,7 +532,6 @@ def _run_gluon_decode(

     v_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
 ) -> None:
-    from aiter import dtypes as aiter_dtypes
     from aiter.ops.triton.gluon.pa_decode_gluon import (
         get_recommended_splits,
         pa_decode_gluon,
@@ -580,7 +579,6 @@ def _run_gluon_decode(
     )
 
     is_fp8 = _is_fp8_kv_cache_tensor(k_cache)
-    compute_type = aiter_dtypes.fp8 if is_fp8 else q.dtype
     if is_fp8:
         if sides_packed and not all(
             scale is None or scale.numel() == 1 for scale in (k_scale, v_scale)
@@ -610,7 +608,8 @@ def _run_gluon_decode(
         query_length=1,
         max_context_partition_num=max_context_partition_num,
         context_partition_size=context_partition_size,
-        compute_type=compute_type,
+        # FP8 compute would round Q and P to e4m3 at no speedup.
+        compute_type=q.dtype,
         query_scale=None,
         key_scale=k_scale_arg,
         value_scale=v_scale_arg,
